categories.main_business_segments: Kakiyasu Honten operates five main business segments: Meat (primarily beef, pork, and chicken retail and processing), Prepared Foods (Western and Chinese-style deli foods, bento, and specialty stores), Japanese Sweets (traditional wagashi such as ohagi and daifuku), Restaurants (including high-end Japanese cuisine, grill, buffet, and food court formats), and Food Products (retort and jarred foods, especially shigure-ni, for retail and gift markets).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes strict hygiene and temperature control in meat processing, with an integrated in-house system from procurement (notably Matsusaka beef and proprietary brands) to retail. Prepared foods and sweets are crafted by skilled artisans focusing on freshness and visual appeal, while shigure-ni products use traditional Kuwana methods for soft, flavorful results. Production employs a combination of traditional Japanese culinary techniques and modern quality management.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Kakiyasu serves a broad consumer base through specialty retail stores in department stores, shopping centers, and highway service areas, as well as through restaurants and food courts. Its key markets are Japanese consumers seeking premium meat, prepared foods, and traditional sweets, with additional B2B sales to supermarkets and high-end retailers for its food products.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates exclusively in Japan, with a network of stores and restaurants spanning major urban and regional centers nationwide. All production facilities and the majority of its retail footprint are located within Japan, with no overseas operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kakiyasu is primarily positioned downstream in the supply chain, focusing on the processing, retail, and direct-to-consumer sale of meat, prepared foods, sweets, and restaurant services. It also engages in some midstream activities through in-house meat processing and food manufacturing.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, the company prioritizes continuous improvement of product quality, cost efficiency, and customer value, while adapting to changing consumer needs through new store formats and product development. There is a strong focus on sustainability, workforce diversity, and operational efficiency, but no significant mention of formal R&D activities or technological innovation initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through direct sales of products (meat, prepared foods, sweets, and food products) at company-operated stores and restaurants, as well as wholesale to retailers. Restaurant operations and gift sales also contribute to the revenue mix.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Kakiyasu competes with other premium meat retailers, deli chains, and Japanese confectionery brands, as well as restaurant operators in the high-end and casual dining segments. It positions itself as a high-quality, tradition-driven brand with a strong reputation in the Japanese food retail and restaurant industry.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending April 2025, consolidated sales were 36.1 billion yen, with operating profit of 1.5 billion yen and net profit of 701 million yen. The company has experienced a recent decline in both sales and profits due to cost pressures and market challenges, with a stable but mature growth profile and a strong equity ratio (78.4%).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kakiyasu differentiates itself through its commitment to quality, tradition, and customer experience, offering premium meats (notably Matsusaka beef), artisanal prepared foods, and authentic Japanese sweets. The company emphasizes freshness, craftsmanship, and hospitality, aiming to deliver high perceived value and trust under the established 'Kakiyasu' brand.
